from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Intuition of Convergence", 
                          ["Standard convergence means getting closer.", 
                           "Distances shrink on a number line.", 
                           "An ant approaches the crumb."])
        
        # Define elements
        target = Dot(color=RED).set_radius(0.15)
        self.place_at_grid(target, 'C4')
        target_label = Text("Target", font_size=20, color=RED).next_to(target, DOWN)
        
        point = Dot(color=WHITE).set_radius(0.1)
        self.place_at_grid(point, 'C2')
        
        seq_label = Text("Sequence", font_size=20, color="#FFCC00")
        self.place_at_grid(seq_label, 'B2')
        seq_label.set_opacity(0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)
        self.play(FadeIn(target), Write(target_label), FadeIn(point))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(BLUE)
        self.play(FadeIn(seq_label))
        self.play(point.animate.move_to(target.get_center() + LEFT * 0.3))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(BLUE)
        self.play(point.animate.move_to(target.get_center() + LEFT * 0.1))
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "P-adic metrics define new distance.", 
            "Divisibility by two measures size.", 
            "High powers mean smaller values.", 
            "Binary trees visualize this structure.", 
            "Eight is smaller than three."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Introducing the 2-adic Metric", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display 2-adic valuation formula |x|_2 = 2^{-v_2(x)}
        formula = MathTex(r"|x|_2 = 2^{-v_2(x)}", color="#00FFCC")
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'B2', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FFCC")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Visualize powers of 2 (2, 4, 8) shrinking
        nums = VGroup(
            Text("2", color=WHITE),
            Text("4", color=WHITE),
            Text("8", color=WHITE)
        ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(nums, 'D2', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(nums))
        
        # Show shrinking
        self.play(
            nums[0].animate.scale(0.8),
            nums[1].animate.scale(0.6),
            nums[2].animate.scale(0.4),
        )
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # High powers mean smaller values
        arrow = Arrow(start=UP, end=DOWN, color="#FF99FF")
        self.place_at_grid(arrow, 'D5', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(GrowArrow(arrow))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF99FF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Binary trees visualize this structure
        # (Placeholder for structure representation)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(BLUE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Eight is smaller than three
        comp = MathTex(r"|8|_2 < |3|_2", color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(comp, 'E3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(comp))
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Infinite Sums in the 2-adic World", [
            "2-adic series converge differently.", 
            "Terms must shrink via divisibility.", 
            "Powers of two settle down.", 
            "The sum equals negative one.", 
            "Infinite sums find stable values."
        ])
        
        # Animations
        # Initialize
        series_tex = MathTex("S = 1 + 2 + 4 + 8 + \\dots", color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(series_tex, 'B1', 'C6', scale_factor=0.8)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.play(FadeIn(series_tex))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        # Highlighting term by term
        term1 = MathTex("1", color="#FFFF00").next_to(series_tex, DOWN)
        term2 = MathTex("+ 2", color="#FFFF00").next_to(term1, RIGHT)
        self.play(FadeIn(term1), FadeIn(term2))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        partial_sums = MathTex("S_n \\to -1", color="#FF00FF")
        self.place_at_grid(partial_sums, 'E3', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(partial_sums))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        # Focus on -1
        self.play(Indicate(partial_sums))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Divergence depends on our metric.", "Real lines explode to infinity.", "2-adic portals capture them."]
        self.setup_layout("Convergence vs. Divergence: The Shift", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        real_line = NumberLine(x_range=[0, 10, 1], length=5).set_color(WHITE)
        adic_line = NumberLine(x_range=[-2, 2, 1], length=5).set_color(WHITE)
        
        # Positioning
        self.place_at_grid(real_line, 'B2', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(adic_line, 'E2', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Labels
        real_label = Text("Real Line", font_size=20).next_to(real_line, UP)
        adic_label = Text("2-adic Tree", font_size=20).next_to(adic_line, UP)
        
        # Divergent sequence (Real)
        real_dots = VGroup(*[Dot(real_line.n2p(2**i), color=RED) for i in range(4)])
        
        # Convergent sequence (2-adic)
        adic_dots = VGroup(*[Dot(adic_line.n2p(-1 + 1/(2**i)), color=GREEN) for i in range(4)])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(real_line), FadeIn(adic_line), FadeIn(real_label), FadeIn(adic_label))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF0000")
        self.play(Create(real_dots))
        self.play(real_dots.animate.shift(RIGHT * 2)) # Visual representation of explosion
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.play(Create(adic_dots))
        self.wait(1)

outline.topic: Exploring the 2-adic Metric: Where Infinite Sums Behave Differently
outline.target_audience: Undergraduate mathematics students or advanced high school students

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Intuition of Convergence
sections.content: Briefly revisit standard Euclidean convergence. Define convergence as 'getting smaller' or 'getting closer.' Use a visual of a point moving toward zero on a number line to illustrate the distance |x - y|.
sections.example: An ant walking toward a crumb: the distance between them shrinks to zero as the ant takes smaller and smaller steps.

sections.title: Introducing the 2-adic Metric
sections.content: Introduce the p-adic perspective. Explain the 2-adic norm |x|_2: a number is 'small' if it is divisible by high powers of 2. Visually represent this as a hierarchical tree structure (the 2-adic tree) where branches represent powers of 2.
sections.example: A 'Binary Sorter' robot that finds a number 'small' if it ends in many zeros in binary (e.g., 8 is 'smaller' than 3 because 8 = 2^3, while 3 = 2^0).

sections.title: Infinite Sums in the 2-adic World
sections.content: Contrast standard convergence with 2-adic convergence. In the 2-adic metric, a series converges if the terms 'shrink' in terms of 2-divisibility. Visually show a series like 1 + 2 + 4 + 8 + ... moving toward a specific 2-adic value.
sections.example: A digital alarm clock that counts in powers of 2; in the 2-adic world, the infinite sum 1 + 2 + 4 + ... actually equals -1.

sections.title: Convergence vs. Divergence: The Shift
sections.content: Explain that series which diverge in standard math (like 1+2+4+...) can converge in the 2-adic metric. Use a split-screen animation showing a divergent path on the real line vs. a convergent path on the 2-adic tree.
sections.example: A 'Dimension Jumper' character: walking along the real line leads to infinity, but stepping into the '2-adic portal' makes the infinite sequence of powers of 2 settle into a single stable point.

sections.title: Summary and Implications
sections.content: Recap the core idea: Convergence depends on how we define distance. By changing the 'ruler' (the metric), the entire landscape of mathematical series changes.
sections.example: A map of the same city drawn with two different scales: one scale highlights roads, the other highlights underground utility pipes.
